title: Marketplace listing: risk, acceptance criteria, and copy primer
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact primer for the cloud marketplace listing preflight that focuses on three often-missed things: (1) risk / non-functional acceptance criteria, (2) the minimal technical dependencies that block approval, and (3) short, testable copy variants for listing pages and tiles.

Context and why this exists:
Past listings passed product review but then hit stalls during legal/compliance or billing integration because we didn’t capture edge-case acceptance criteria early. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — a checklist + copy templates + owners — to hand to a partner or internal enablement lead to run the last-mile prep.

High-level scope (what this doc covers)
- Marketplace types: AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace (SaaS listings and marketplace metered billing).
- Listing assets: tile image, short tagline, 1–3 sentence description, 3–5 feature bullets, pricing & SKU mapping notes, legal boilerplate pointers.
- Non-functional acceptance: availability SLOs, telemetry hooks, support escalation, data residency disclosures, and rollback/fallback policies.

Quick triage (go/no-go signals)
- Immediate blockers (fail fast):
  - No linked billing SKU or billing owner identified (owner: Finance) — BLOCK
  - No security questionnaire/attestation for target marketplace (owner: Security) — BLOCK
  - Required marketplace integrations (license entitlements, metering hooks) unimplemented in staging (owner: Eng) — BLOCK
- High risk but negotiable:
  - Partial observability (basic metrics present but traces absent) — mitigatable with post-launch instrumentation plan
  - Incomplete region coverage (e.g., no EU region for EU-targeted listing) — mitigatable with stall notes and cross-region availability policy

Technical acceptance checklist (must be explicit for engineering handoffs)
- Billing and metering:
  - Assigned SKU(s) and pricing tier mapping document (filename + owner).
  - Metering endpoints implemented and verified in staging (sample payload, success/error codes).
  - End-to-end billing test passes using marketplace sandbox account.
- Authentication & entitlements:
  - SSO/OAuth flow validated (if required by marketplace) and documented steps to reproduce.
  - API keys and secrets lifecycle plan documented (rotation, storage).
- Deployment & region coverage:
  - Images/containers registered in marketplace-required registries (if required).
  - Region flags: list of supported regions with fallbacks; confirm data residency statements.
- Observability & support:
  - Exported metrics (latency, request rate, error rate) with retention window required by marketplace.
  - Error budget thresholds agreed and onboarded into SRE runbooks.
  - Support contact, escalation steps, and on-call rotation mapping.
- Security & compliance:
  - Completed marketplace security checklist (attach questionnaire).
  - Any required pen-test or attestation scheduled or completed.
- Release controls:
  - Canary rollout plan and auto-fallback policy documented (who flips the switch, rollback runbook).
  - Post-launch smoke test script and owner.

Acceptance criteria (pass -> list goes live):
1) Billing: sandbox metering tests green, finance sign-off on SKU mapping.
2) Security: required attestation uploaded, Security review "OK for marketplace".
3) Technical: metering endpoints + auth flows verified in staging; basic observability enabled.
4) Legal: marketplace contract template reviewed and standard terms accepted or redlines captured.
5) Copy: final short and long descriptions provided and localized for target regions if necessary.

Risk register (short form)
- Risk: Metering quotas undercount due to upstream caching. Impact: revenue bleed and reconciliation work. Mitigation: include unique invoice id in metering payload; reconcile daily for the first 30 days. Owner: Finance/Eng.
- Risk: EU customers require explicit data residency statement and we initially only have us-west region. Impact: listing rejected or customers blocked. Mitigation: Declare limited region availability in listing and add roadmap timeline for EU. Owner: Product.
- Risk: Marketplace legal asks for indemnity language we cannot accept. Impact: delay in approval. Mitigation: Legal pre-review and escalation path. Owner: Legal/GTM.

Copy primer (short variants ready to drop into forms)
- Tile tagline (8–10 words):
  - "Low-latency LLM inference platform with predictable costs"
  - "Production-grade LLM serving with integrated observability"
  - "Scale LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"

- One-line product blurb (for hero line / 1-liner):
  - "Redwood Inference: production LLM serving that balances latency, cost, and reliability across hosted and private deployments."
  - "Deploy and operate LLMs with predictable performance — hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, or private VPC."

- 3-bullet feature highlights (concise, benefit-first):
  - "Fast hosted API and streaming responses — get to market quickly."
  - "Reserved dedicated capacity with SLA-backed latency and throughput."
  - "Private deployments with VPC and KMS integrations for regulated workloads."

- Short customer benefit statements (for tile tooltips):
  - "Reduce per-token cost with intelligent batching and caching."
  - "Stay online under load with automatic fallbacks and rollouts."
  - "Centralized observability for per-route latency and token-level cost insights."

Tone & style notes (for GC and localization folks)
- Use measurable language (latency, cost, SLA) when possible; avoid vague claims like "industry-leading" unless we have a benchmark link.
- Keep sentences short for marketplace UI constraints (some fields truncate aggressively).
- Prepare a secondary, privacy-friendly variant for EU/GDPR contexts that omits usage-data examples.

Preflight tasks (owner + target date)
- Finance: finalize SKU mapping and metering plan — due 2025-02-20 (owner: Liam Chen).
- Security: attach marketplace questionnaire v1 and confirm outstanding items — due 2025-02-17 (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- Eng: run sandbox metering tests + provide sample payloads — due 2025-02-18 (owner: Jordan Reyes).
- Legal: review marketplace contract redlines — due 2025-02-21 (owner: Legal).
- GTM: finalize tile assets (2 size variants) and final copy — due 2025-02-19 (owner: Aisha Martinez).

Open questions and decisions needed
- Do we want to offer a free trial via the marketplace metering flow, or route trials to hosted account creation? (tradeoffs: friction vs. billing complexity). Owner: Growth Team.
- If a partner requests longer data retention for logs for troubleshooting, what is the default retention and who approves exceptions? Owner: Security/SRE.
- Localization: which languages do we prioritize at launch (EN, DE, FR)? Owner: GTM.

Rollback/incident playbook (summary)
- If marketplace metering errors >1% over a 10m window AND customer impact spike observed:
  1) Flip routing to fallback model variant (pre-agreed compatible SKU). Owner: Oncall Eng.
  2) Pause acceptance of new marketplace provisionings (control plane toggle). Owner: Ops.
  3) Notify marketplace account manager and legal if SLA threshold breached. Owner: GTM/Legal.

Deliverables to attach for submission
- Tile image (png) 600x360 and 240x144
- 1-line and 3-line descriptions (final)
- Billing SKU matrix + sample metering payloads
- Security questionnaire PDF and SRE runbook excerpt
- Support contact & escalation spreadsheet

Change log:
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-02-13: added technical acceptance checklist after sync with Jordan
- 2025-02-17: security notes updated (Priya)
- 2025-02-18: copy variants refined and action owners added

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add localized copy and store variants in repo path: github.com/redwood/marketplace-assets/locales
- Create a short demo video for marketplace listing tile (30s) to improve conversion — track in Jira GO-1123
- Verify marketplace-specific image size constraints for GCP Marketplace (sometimes different).

If you're the person running the checklist: print the acceptance criteria section and run through each item with the named owner before submitting. If anything is ambiguous, escalate to the GTM PM (owner: Aisha Martinez).

End of primer.
